key: ‘Thou knowest how that David my father could not build a house for the name of the LORD his God for the wars which were about him on every side, until the LORD put them under the soles of my feet.
s: Sending to Hiram of Tyre for cedars, Solomon explains why the Temple falls to him; Radak, on 5:17, reads the wars as the apparent reason, Solomon keeping from Hiram that God had withheld the task from David, which would not honour his father.
src: Radak, Commentary on 1 Kings, on 1 Kings 5:17, Hebrew (Radak on Nach), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

reason: verse.js ok, ref 1 Kings 5:17 and at [291,17] match. Plain sense faithful: 5:16 to 20 are Solomon’s message to Hiram asking for cedars of Lebanon for the house for the LORD’s name; no four-word run from the key. Radak’s own words on 5:17 (lemma mipnei hamilhamah): Solomon did not wish to reveal that God had prevented David, as it was not to his father’s honour, and gave this apparent reason; the sentence carries this. Considered naming Rashi (not permitted because of the war, citing the rest-before-the-place rule of Deuteronomy 12:10 to 11), but Radak himself gives that same rule on 5:18, so the two do not genuinely differ and the single commentator stands. A two-name draft was gated (scratch/V-d107-p.json) and set aside for that reason. entry-check ok on scratch/V-L3pri-d107-p.json.
